newsitem.title: USA: Overnight cold skirts Mexico coffee - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: Overnight cold skirts Mexico coffee - Smith Barney.

text.p: Temperatures remained above freezing early Thursday morning in Mexico's coffee belt, sparing the region's coffee trees of any damaging frost, Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said.
But with readings expected to fall back toward the freezing mark again early Friday, the threat to coffee was not yet over, Davis said in his daily weather update.
"Temps overnight did not drop low enough to cause any significant damage to the crop," Davis said. "Lows this morning were mainly in the mid 30s to mid 40s."
Extensive cloud-cover prevented temperatures from falling to critical levels, he said.
That cloud cover was likely to dissipate by Friday morning, however, pushing the thermostat to a low of 32 degrees Fahrenheit (0 Celsius) in the northern fringe of the belt, he said.

"Temps will be a bit cooler during the next few mornings than this morning due to the more favorable radiational cooling," he said. "Thus, there may be some frost in the far northern sections of the belt and this could result in some isolated pockets of minor damage."
No problems were foreseen for the central and southern portions of the belt.
While another cold snap is expected to hit the U.S. next week, the coldest air should not move south into Mexico as it did this week, he said.

"At this current time, the big Arctic outbreak next week does not look like a major threat to the coffee in Mexico," he said. "It does need to be monitored for any changes but, at this time it does not look like a damage threat."
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
